newsitem.title: FINLAND: Buoyant Nokia takes lively Helsinki up one pct.
newsitem.headline: Buoyant Nokia takes lively Helsinki up one pct.

text.p: Shares ended another lively session up for a fourth straight day on Friday, with Nokia extending Thursday's gains to lift the main indices by one percent, in otherwise more mixed trade than of late.
Brokers, citing another sunny start in Wall St, were again confident bulls would prevail next week.
The FOX index rose 1.06 percent to 1,222.03, up 1.5 percent on the week, with the all-share HEX up 0.99 percent to 3,543.49. Volume was again very hefty for July at 700 million markka.
"This isn't over yet," one broker said of the uptrend, as the Dow industrials opened higher.
Nokia closed 5.40 markka higher at 449.90, off an intraday high 455.00, which was just three markka short of its July 17 all-time high. It accounted for almost half the total volume.

Nokia continued to draw strength from Swedish rival Ericsson's above-forecast first-half earnings report, which sparked strong gains in both shares on Thursday, brokers said. Analysts said on Thursday expectations for Nokia's H1 had risen.
"If Ericsson can do it, then why not Nokia?," one broker said, noting that Nokia is even bigger in the mobile phone business than Ericsson, whose H1 mobile sales doubled.
But the bank still ended the week 11 percent up, lifted by a spate of overseas buying fuelled by recent recommendations and talk of more consolidation in the Nordic sector.

Insurers -- said by analysts to be more likely merger candidates short-term -- took the baton from Merita. Pohjola added 8.00 markka to 172.00, Sampo rose 21.50 to 579.00. But one broker noted the real attraction may have been their considerable Nokia holdings.
Finnair rose more than seven percent in brisk demand, ending up 2.90 markka at 43.90, boosted by recent recommendations after clearing a psychological 40.00 markka barrier on Wednesday.
